Package org.geysermc.paletter

Class VanillaContent

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.VanillaContent
public final class VanillaContent extends Object
Selects which vanilla content exists, configured in Paletter.Builder#vanilla. A removed item is not registered: it has no definition and no creative entry, and resolves through the Fallbacks. Blocks are never removed, the client's block palette has to match; a block that is missing resolves through the fallbacks as well.

Content a version has only behind an experiment toggle (BDS offers it only to worlds with that experiment, see experiments) is missing unless the toggle is enabled, so ordinary (non-forced) fallbacks apply to it.

Since:
1.0.0

    • experiments

      public @NonNull VanillaContent experiments(@NonNull String... toggles)
      Sets the enabled experiment toggles (e.g. y_2026_drop_4). By default none is enabled: the items and blocks a version has only behind a toggle are missing in its palette, so the Fallbacks apply to them like to content the version lacks altogether (and force is only for content that is really there). An enabled toggle makes its content present in the versions that gate it; those palettes list the toggle in Palette.experiments() and send it with Palette.applyTo(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.packet.StartGamePacket). A palette tells the toggle of a piece of content with Palette#experimentOf, and its report has a line for every toggle left disabled.
      Parameters:
      toggles - the toggle ids, as BDS names them
